Effundam spiritum meum super semen tuum, et benedictionem meam super germina tua.<div eID="gen48707" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen48708" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">4.</hi> And they shall spring up <hi type="italic">as </hi>among the grass, as willows by the water courses.<div eID="gen48708" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen48709" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">4.</hi> Et germinabunt quasi inter herbam, quasi salices juxta rivos aquarum.<div eID="gen48709" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen48710" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">5.</hi> One shall say, I <hi type="italic">am</hi> the LORD’S; and another shall call <hi type="italic">himself </hi>by the name of Jacob; and another shall subscribe <hi type="italic">with </hi>his hand unto the LORD, and surname <hi type="italic">himself </hi>by the name of Israel.<div eID="gen48710" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen48711" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">5.</hi> Hic dicet, Ego sum Iehovae; et ille vocabitur nomine Iacob; altus scribet manu sua, Iehovae (sum), et nomine Israel cognominabitur.<div eID="gen48711" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen48712" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">6.</hi> Thus saith the LORD the King of Israel, and his redeemer the LORD of hosts; I<hi type="italic"> am </hi>the first, and I <hi type="italic">am</hi> the last; and besides me <hi type="italic">there is </hi>no God.<div eID="gen48712" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen48713" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">6.</hi> Sic dicit Iehova, rex Israel, et redemptor ejus, Iehova exercituum: Ego primus, et idem novissimus, et praeter me non est Deus.<div eID="gen48713" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen48714" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">7.</hi> And who, as I, shall call, and shall declare it, and set it in order for me, since I appointed the ancient people? and the things that are coming, and shall come, let them shew unto them.<div eID="gen48714" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen48715" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">7.</hi> Et quis sicut ego vocabit, annunciabit hoc, et ordinabit hoc mihi, ex quo constitui populum seculi? Et quae pendent, et quae ventura sunt, illis annuncient.<div eID="gen48715" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen48716" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">8.</hi> Fear ye not, neither be afraid: have not I told thee from that time, and have declared <hi type="italic">it? </hi>ye <hi type="italic">are </hi>even my witnesses. Is there a God besides me? yea, <hi type="italic">there is </hi>no God; I know not <hi type="italic">any.</hi><div eID="gen48716" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen48717" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">8.</hi> Ne timeatis et ne terreamini. An non ex tune audire to feci, et annuntiavi? Itaque vos testes mei, quod non sit Deus praeter me, et non sit fortis quem ignorem.<div eID="gen48717" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen48718" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">9.</hi> They that make a graven image <hi type="italic">are </hi>all of them vanity; and their delectable things shall not profit; and they <hi type="italic">are </hi>their own witnesses; they see not, nor know; that they may be ashamed.<div eID="gen48718" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen48719" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">9.</hi> Fictores sculptilis omnes vanitas; et desiderabilia eorum nihil prosunt; et testes eorum ipsi, quod non vident, nec cognoscunt; ideoque confundentur.<div eID="gen48719" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen48720" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">10.</hi> Who hath formed a god, or molten a graven image <hi type="italic">that</hi> is profitable for nothing?<div eID="gen48720" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen48721" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">10.</hi> Quis formator Dei? et quis sculptilis confiator, quod nullam ad rem usui est?<div eID="gen48721" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen48722" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">11.</hi> Behold, all his fellows shall be ashamed: and the workmen, they <hi type="italic">are </hi>of men: let them all be gathered together, let them stand up; <hi type="italic">yet </hi>they shall fear, <hi type="italic">and </hi>they shall be ashamed together.<div eID="gen48722" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen48723" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">11.</hi> Ecce omnes socii ejus pudefient, et artifices ipsi sunt ex hominibus. Ut conveniant omnes, ac stent, pavebunt, et pudefient simul.<div eID="gen48723" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen48724" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">12.</hi> The smith with the tongs both worketh in the coals, and fashioneth it with hammers, and worketh it with the strength of his arms: yea, he is hungry, and his strength faileth: he drinketh no water, and is faint.<div eID="gen48724" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen48725" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">12.</hi> Faber ferrarius limam <hi type="italic">(aut forcipem) </hi>sumet; operabitur in prunis, malleis formabit illud; operabitur in eo, brachio virtutis suae; etiam famelicus, ut deficiant rites; non bibat aquam, ut fatiscat.<div eID="gen48725" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen48726" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">13.</hi> The carpenter stretcheth out <hi type="italic">his </hi>rule; he marketh it out with a line; he fitteth it with planes, and he marketh it out with the compass, and maketh it after the figure of a man, according to the beauty of a man; that it may remain in the house.<div eID="gen48726" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen48727" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">13.</hi> Faber lignarius extendit regulam, illud delineat filo tincto, aptat planulis, circino figurat; facit illud secundum formam viri, secundum effigiem hominis, ut sedeat in domo.<div eID="gen48727" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen48728" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">14.</hi> He heweth him down cedars, and taketh the cypress and the oak, which he strengtheneth for himself among the trees of the forest: he planteth an ash, and the rain doth nourish <hi type="italic">it.</hi><div eID="gen48728" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen48729" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">14.</hi> Succidet sibi cedros, tollet ilicem et quercum; roborabitur ad ligna silvae; plantabit pinum, quam pluvia enutriet.<div eID="gen48729" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen48730" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">15.</hi> Then shall it be for a man to burn: for he will take thereof, and warm himself; yea, he kindleth <hi type="italic">it, </hi>and baketh bread; yea, he maketh a god, and worshippeth <hi type="italic">it: </hi>he maketh it a graven image, and falleth down thereto.<div eID="gen48730" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen48731" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">15.</hi> Tum erit homini in incendium; nam accipiet ex illis, et calefaciet se; praeterea furnum accendet, et coquet panes; Deum quoque efficiet, atque adorabit; finget idolum, et prosternet se coram co.<div eID="gen48731" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen48732" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">16.</hi> He burneth part thereof in the fire; with part thereof he eateth flesh; he roasteth roast, and is satisfied: yea, he warmeth <hi type="italic">himself, </hi>and saith, Aha, I am warm, I have seen the fire:<div eID="gen48732" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen48733" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">16.</hi> Partem ejus comburet igni; ex parte carnem comedet; assabit assaturam, et saturabitur. Deinde calefaciet se, ac dicet, Ohe calefactus sum, et vidi ignem.<div eID="gen48733" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen48734" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">17.</hi> And the residue thereof he maketh a god, <hi type="italic">even </hi>his graven image: he falleth down unto it, and worshippeth <hi type="italic">it, </hi>and prayeth unto it, and saith, Deliver me; for thou <hi type="italic">art </hi>my god.<div eID="gen48734" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen48735" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">17.</hi> Reliquias ejus in Deum vertit in sculptile suum; incurvat se coram eo; adorat et precatur illud, dicens, Libera me, quia Deus meus es.<div eID="gen48735" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen48736" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">18.</hi> They have not known nor understood: for he hath shut their eyes, that they cannot see; <hi type="italic">and </hi>their hearts, that they cannot understand.<div eID="gen48736" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen48737" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">18.</hi> Nescierunt, nec intellexerunt; quia oblevit oculos eorum, ne videant, et cor eorum, ne intelligant.<div eID="gen48737" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen48738" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">19.</hi> And none considereth in his heart, neither <hi type="italic">is there </hi>knowledge nor understanding to say, I have burned part of it in the fire; yea, also I have baked bread upon the coals thereof; I have roasted flesh, and eaten <hi type="italic">it: </hi>and shall I make the residue thereof an abomination? shall I fall down to the stock of a tree?<div eID="gen48738" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen48739" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">19.</hi> Non redit ad cor suum, non est sensus, nec intelligentia, ut dicat, Partem ejus combussi igni; etiam super prunas ejus coxi panem; assavi carnem, et comedi; residuum ejus in abominationem vertam: coram trunco ligni incurvabo me?<div eID="gen48739" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen48740" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">20.</hi> He feedeth on ashes: a deceived heart hath turned him aside, that he cannot deliver his soul, nor say, <hi type="italic">Is there </hi>not a lie in my right hand?<div eID="gen48740" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen48741" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">20.</hi> Pascit cinerem, cor seductum inclinat eum, ut non liberet animam suam, neque dicat, Annon mendacium in dextera mea?<div eID="gen48741" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen48742" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">21.</hi> Remember these, O Jacob and Israel; for thou <hi type="italic">art </hi>my servant: I have formed thee; thou <hi type="italic">art </hi>my servant: O Israel, thou shalt not be forgotten of me.<div eID="gen48742" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen48743" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">21.</hi> Memor esto horum, Iacob, et Israel, quia servus meus es; formavi to; servus meus es; Israel, ne obliviscaris mei.<div eID="gen48743" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen48744" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">22.</hi> I have blotted out, as a thick cloud, thy transgressions, and, as a cloud, thy sins: return unto me; for I have redeemed thee.<div eID="gen48744" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen48745" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">22.</hi> Delevi, ut nubem, iniquitates tuas; ut nebulam, peccata tua. Revertere ad me, quia redemi to.<div eID="gen48745" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen48746" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">23.</hi> Sing, O ye heavens; for the LORD hath done <hi type="italic">it: </hi>shout, ye lower parts of the earth: break forth into singing, ye mountains, O forest, and every tree therein: for the LORD hath redeemed Jacob, and glorified himself in Israel.<div eID="gen48746" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen48747" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">23.</hi> Laudate, coeli, quia fecit Iehova; jubilate, inferiora terrae; erumpite, montes, in laudem; silva et omnis arbor quae in ea st; quoniam redemit Iehova Iacob, et in Israel glorificabitur.<div eID="gen48747" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen48748" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">24.</hi> Thus saith the LORD, thy redeemer, and he that formed thee from the womb, I <hi type="italic">am</hi> the LORD that maketh all <hi type="italic">things; </hi>that stretcheth forth the heavens alone; that spreadeth abroad the earth by myself;<div eID="gen48748" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen48749" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">24.</hi> Sic dicit Iehova redemptor tuns, et factor tuus ex utero. Ego Iehova faciens omnia, extendens coelos solus, expandens terrain inca virtute (<hi type="italic">vel, a meipso.)</hi><div eID="gen48749" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen48750" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">25.</hi> That frustrateth the tokens of the liars, and maketh diviners mad; that turneth wise <hi type="italic">men </hi>backward, and maketh their knowledge foolish;<div eID="gen48750" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen48751" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">25.</hi> Dissipans signa divinatorum, ariolos dementans, convertens sapientes retrorsum, et scientiam corum infatuans.<div eID="gen48751" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen48752" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">26.</hi> That confirmeth the word of his servant, and performeth the counsel of his messengers; that saith to Jerusalem, Thou shalt be inhabited; and to the cities of Judah, Ye shall be built, and I will raise up the decayed places thereof:<div eID="gen48752" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen48753" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">26.</hi> Suscitans verbum servi sui, et consilium nuntiorum suorum perficiens; dicens Ierosolymae, Habitaberis; et civitatibus Iuda, Extruemini; et ruinas ejus erigam.<div eID="gen48753" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen48754" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">27.</hi> That saith to the deep, Be dry, and I will dry up thy rivers:<div eID="gen48754" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen48755" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">27.</hi> Dicens profundo, Exsiccare, et flumina tua arefaeiam.<div eID="gen48755" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen48756" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">28.</hi> That saith of Cyrus, <hi type="italic">He is </hi>my shepherd, and shall perform all my pleasure: even saying to Jerusalem, Thou shalt be built; and to the temple, Thy foundation shall be laid.<div eID="gen48756" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen48757" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">28.</hi> Dicens Cyro, Pastor meus; et omnem voluntatem meam perficiet; dicendo etiam Ierosolymae, Aedificaberis; et templo, Fundaberis.<div eID="gen48757" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row> </table> <div sID="gen48758" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen48758" type="x-p"/>

<ns0:div xmlns:ns0="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="43" type="chapter">
                  <ns0:head>CHAP. XLIII.</ns0:head>
                  <ns0:p n="1">1 BUt now thus saith the LORD <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">But notwithstanding thy gross insensibleness under for<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mer judgments, for which I might justly send far heavier ones upon thee, yet I will deal mercifully with thee.</ns0:note> that cre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ated thee <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">That made thee his people, and that in so miraculous a manner, as if he had created thee a second time out of nothing; and th<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>refore he will be gracious to his own workmanship.</ns0:note>, O Jacob, and he that for<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />med thee, O Israel, Fear not: for I have re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />deemed thee <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">From the <ns0:hi>Egyptians,</ns0:hi> and divers other enemies; and there<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore I will redeem thee again.</ns0:note>, I have called <ns0:hi>thee</ns0:hi> by thy name <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">By the name of <ns0:hi>Gods People,</ns0:hi> which was as proper and peculiar to them, as the name of <ns0:hi>Israel.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>, thou <ns0:hi>art</ns0:hi> mine.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="2">2 When thou <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 66. 12.</ns0:note> passest through the waters, <ns0:hi>I will be</ns0:hi> with thee: and through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee: when thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be burnt; neither shall the flame kindle upon thee <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Though I will chastise thee for thy sins, yet I will not suffer thine enemies utterly to destroy thee, Compare, <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 30. 11.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="3">3 For I <ns0:hi>am</ns0:hi> the LORD thy God, the holy One of Israel, thy saviour: <ns0:hi>I</ns0:hi> gave Egypt <ns0:hi>for</ns0:hi> thy ransom <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">This was fulfilled either, 1. When God smote the <ns0:hi>Egyptians,</ns0:hi> both first-born and others in <ns0:hi>Egypt;</ns0:hi> and drown<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed <ns0:hi>Pharoah,</ns0:hi> and his Host in the Red Sea, for the safety and benefit of his people: Or, 2. When the King of <ns0:hi>As<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />syria,</ns0:hi> either <ns0:hi>Sennacherib,</ns0:hi> as many think, or rather <ns0:hi>Esar<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                              <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                           </ns0:gap>had<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />don,</ns0:hi> who designed to revenge his Fathers disgrace, and loss before <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> upon the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> but was diverted and di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rected by God to employ his Forces against <ns0:hi>Egypt,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Ethiopia,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Seba,</ns0:hi> as it follows. See the Notes upon <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 20. 1, &c.</ns0:note>, Ethiopia and Seba <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">The <ns0:hi>Sabaeians</ns0:hi> who were confederate with the <ns0:hi>Ethiopians,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Cushites.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> for thee.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="4">4 Since thou wast precious in my sight, thou hast been honourable, and <ns0:hi>I</ns0:hi> have loved thee <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>o the sence is, From that time that I chose thee for my precious and peculiar treasure and People, I have had a great esteem and affection for thee. But the words may well be, and by some are rendred thus, <ns0:hi>since that</ns0:hi> (or, <ns0:hi>For that:</ns0:hi> or, Because) <ns0:hi>Thou wast precious in my sight, thou wast honourable,</ns0:hi> (the same thing repeated in other words,) <ns0:hi>and I love thee.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>; therefore will <ns0:hi>I</ns0:hi> give men for thee <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">As I did give up the <ns0:hi>Egyptians,</ns0:hi> and so I am ready to give up others to save thee, as occasion re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />quires.</ns0:note>, and peo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple for thy <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> person.</ns0:note> 
                     <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> soul.</ns0:note> life.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="5">5 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 44. 1, 2 Jer. 30. 10. & 46. 27.</ns0:note> Fear not, for <ns0:hi>I am</ns0:hi> with thee; I will bring thy seed from the east, and gather thee from the west <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Although the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> shall for their sins be carried cap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tives out of their own Land Northward and Eastward into <ns0:hi>Babylon,</ns0:hi> and the adjacent Countries, and others of them shall flee Southward and Westward, and shall there pine away in their iniquities, as I threatned; yet their posterity I will bring back into <ns0:hi>Canaan,</ns0:hi> from all the places where they are dispersed.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="6">6 <ns0:hi>I</ns0:hi> will say to the north, Give up <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Thou who hast so long had and held my people in Bondage, resign them to me, and permit them to return to their own Land. He speaks either to the Countries themselves by a Prosopopaeia: Or, to the Inhabitants of them.</ns0:note>; and to the south, keep not back; bring my sons <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Do not onely permit but assist and further their return.</ns0:note> from far, and my daughters from the ends of the earth.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="7">7 <ns0:hi>Even</ns0:hi> every one <ns0:hi>that is</ns0:hi> called by my name <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>They are called by my Name.</ns0:hi> I own them for my Peo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple and Children; and therefore what kindness or cruelty you exercise to them, I take it as done to my self. So it is an argument to move those people to let their Cap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tives go: Or, it is an argument to confirm the faith of Gods People, that God would deliver them, because they are his own.</ns0:note>: for <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 100. 3. Chap. 29. 23. Joh. 3. 4, 5. 2 Cor. 5. 17. Eph. 2. 10.</ns0:note> 
                     <ns0:hi>I</ns0:hi> have created him for my glory <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">And therefore I will glorify my Power and goodness, and faithfulness in delivering them.</ns0:note>, <ns0:hi>I</ns0:hi> have formed him, yea, <ns0:hi>I</ns0:hi> have made him <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">I have not onely <ns0:hi>created</ns0:hi> them out of nothing, as I did all other people, but I have also <ns0:hi>formed</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>made</ns0:hi> them my peculiar People.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="8">8 Bring forth the blind People that have eyes,<ns0:note place="margin">* Chap. 42. 19. Ezek. 12. 2.</ns0:note> and the deaf that have ears <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">The sence is either. 1. Bring out of Captivity my peo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple who were blind and deaf, but now have their eyes and ears opened by my grace. So this verse relates to the fore<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />going passages: Or rather, 2. O ye Idolatrous <ns0:hi>Gentiles,</ns0:hi> produce or bring forth your false Gods, which have eyes but see not, and ears but hear not, as is said, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 115. 5, 6. So this verse belongs to the following context, in which God reneweth his contest with Idols; which in this verse he calleth <ns0:hi>blind,</ns0:hi> and in the next verse proveth them so to be.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="9">
                     <ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:603" />9 Let all the Nations be gathered together, and let the people be assembled <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">To plead the cause of their Idols with me.</ns0:note>: <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 41. 21. 22.</ns0:note> who among them can declare this <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">This wonderful work of mine in bringing my people out of Captivity, which I have already foretold, and shall further declare; and that so exactly, that I shall name the person by whom this work shall be begun, even <ns0:hi>Cyrus,</ns0:hi> who is yet un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />born, and shall be so for above 200 years; let any of your Heathen Gods do the like.</ns0:note>, and shew us for<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mer things <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">Not things already past, but such things as shall happen long before the return from the Captivity, which yet your blind Idols cannot foresee. See on <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 41. 22.</ns0:note>? let them bring forth their witnes<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ses <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">Who can testify the truth and certainty of any such predictions of theirs.</ns0:note>, that they may be justified <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">That they may be owned for true Gods, which in that case I allow them to expect. But of this argument see on <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 41. 22, 23.</ns0:note>; or let them hear and say, <ns0:hi>It is</ns0:hi> truth <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">Or if they can produce no evidence of any such thing, as I am well assured that they cannot, let them be silent, and hear me and my witnesses, as it follows in the next verse; and let them confess, that what I say is truth, that I onely am the true God, and that they are but vanity and fals<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hood.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="10">10 Ye <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> my witnesses <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">They can produce no witnesses for themselves, but you my people are able to witness for me, that I have giv<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />en you many plain demonstrations of my certain foreknow<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ledge of future events, by my predictions and promises de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />livered to you from time to time.</ns0:note>, saith the LORD, and my servant whom I have chosen <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Either, 1. <ns0:hi>Isaiah,</ns0:hi> and other Prophets, the singular word being put Collectively: Or, 2. <ns0:hi>Cyrus,</ns0:hi> who is an eminent instance and proof of Gods foreknowledge: Or, 3. the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> as not onely Christi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ans but even the <ns0:hi>Chaldee</ns0:hi> Paraphrast understands it; who is called by this very title, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 42. 1. who also is the most eminent witness in this cause; and that both passively, as he and the time and place, and other circumstances of his birth, and life, and death were particularly foretold by God in Scripture; and actively, as many future things were foretold by Christ, of which we have many examples in the New Testament.</ns0:note>: that ye may know and believe me, and understand that I <ns0:hi>am</ns0:hi> he <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">He of whom the present dispute is, or <ns0:hi>he whom</ns0:hi> I have affirmed my self to be. That I onely am that true God whom we are now seeking in this debate.</ns0:note>: <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 41. 4. & 44. 8.</ns0:note> before me there was <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> nothing formed of God.</ns0:note> no God formed, neither shall there be after me <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">The Gods of the Heathens neither had a being before me nor shall continue after me. Wherein more is understood than is expressed, That whereas the Lord is God from everlasting to everlasting, these false pretenders to the Deity, are but of yesterday, and shall shortly be abolished. And withal he calleth them <ns0:hi>Formed Gods,</ns0:hi> in way of contempt, and to shew the ridicu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lousness of their pretence to the Divinity, which are for<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />med by the hands of men.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="11">11 I, <ns0:hi>even</ns0:hi> I <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 45. 21 Hos. 13. 4.</ns0:note> 
                     <ns0:hi>am</ns0:hi> the LORD, and besides me <ns0:hi>there</ns0:hi> is no saviour <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">That can and doth save his Worshippers; Whereby he implies, that the false Gods were not onely weak and unable to save their people, but also were the destroyers of their people, as being the great cause of their ruine.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="12">12 I have declared, and have saved <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">I first foretold your deliverance, and then effected it.</ns0:note>, and I have shewed <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">I foretold it. This branch he repeated, because this is the principal argument used here, and Chapter 41. to de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />termine this controversy between God and Idols.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Deut. 32. 12.</ns0:note> when <ns0:hi>there was</ns0:hi> no strange <ns0:hi>god</ns0:hi> among you <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">And this I did when you did not worship any Idols, and there<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore it could not be pretended that you had this knowledge from them.</ns0:note>: therefore ye <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> my witnesses, saith the LORD, that I <ns0:hi>am</ns0:hi> God.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="13">13 Yea, <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> from the day.</ns0:note> before the day <ns0:hi>was</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Before all time: Or, which is all one, from all eterni<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ty: Or, <ns0:hi>Since the day</ns0:hi> was, Since the Beginning of time and things, in all ages since the creation of the world</ns0:note>, I <ns0:hi>am</ns0:hi> he <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">I am God, and I have proved my self to be so.</ns0:note>, and <ns0:hi>there is</ns0:hi> none <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">None of those which are called Gods.</ns0:note>, that can deliver out of my hand <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">That can save them whom I will destroy. Therefore they are impotent, and consequently no Gods.</ns0:note>: I will work, and who shall <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> turn it back.</ns0:note> 
                     <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Job 9. 12. Chap. 14. 27. & 46. 10.</ns0:note> let it <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Nor can they hinder me in any other work which I resolve to do.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="14">14 Thus saith the LORD your Redeemer, the holy One of Israel, For your sake I have sent to Babylon <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">I have sent <ns0:hi>Cyrus,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Medes</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Persians</ns0:hi> with him to war against <ns0:hi>Babylon,</ns0:hi> to this very end and purpose, that he might deliver you out of captivity, and restore you to your Land according to my promise.</ns0:note>, and have brought down <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">From that height of Power and glory to which they were advanced.</ns0:note> all their <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">

                  <ns0:p n="18">18 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 46. 9.</ns0:note> Remember ye not the former things, neither consider the things of old <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">But although your former deliverance out of <ns0:hi>Egypt</ns0:hi> was in it self a most glorious work, which you ought al<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />wayes to remember and consider, yet this other work of your deliverance out of <ns0:hi>Babylon</ns0:hi> by <ns0:hi>Cyrus,</ns0:hi> and those bles<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sings which shall follow upon it, and particularly that in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />estimable mercy of sending the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> shall be so tran<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />scendent a favour, that in comparison thereof, all your for<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mer deliverances are scarce worthy of your remembrance and consideration.
